The most likely corrupted element is **Cc**. The residual ringing (7–10 µs settling fails at 0.017 V against a 0.01 V limit) points to weak damping of the loop, and the Miller compensation capacitor sets that damping. Its value, 0.705 pF, looks unusually small compared with the other sizes, which suggests it was scaled down. The DC metrics (output error, feedback ratio, line/load regulation, PSRR at 1 kHz, quiescent current) are all consistent with a correct feedback network and bias, so the fault is most likely in the dynamic path.

The tail mirror M5/M6 (width ratio 2.326/2 ≈ 1.16) is the second candidate, since a wrong mirror ratio shifts the error-amplifier gm and therefore the loop crossover. The pass device Mp is third, because its gate capacitance and gm set the second pole that Cc has to split from the dominant one.
